enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
936 PM MST Tue Nov 10 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... Updated at 934 PM MST Tue Nov 10 2026

 - Dry conditions and light winds persist through the work week
   with typical mid-November temperatures. Some patchy lowland 
   fog is expected again late tonight/early Wednesday morning.

 - Next system arrives late on Friday, bringing rain chances and
   high elevation snow through Saturday night.

 - Slight chance of showers mid portion of next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 934 PM MST Tue Nov 10 2026

Upper low now over northeast Texas with trough hanging back across 
the Big Bend. Moisture with the low is now well east of the area.
Deep layer of moisture well south of our area persists, associated 
with the sub-tropical jet. Northerly mid-level flow and westerly 
upper-level flow has ushered in much drier air (KEPZ PW on 00Z 
sounding down to .43 inches). High amplitude ridge continues 
building in as the aforementioned trough dissipates ahead of the 
ridge. Main Pacific upper low over southern Gulf of Alaska is the 
driver of the building ridge as it digs southward over the next 48 
hours. Thus through Thursday, expect mostly clear skies, light 
winds, and seasonable temperatures.

Friday through Sunday...Pacific low system moves to our area through 
this period. Main Gulf of Alaska low moves onshore of the Pac NW, 
while a secondary low forms much further south, moving across the 
northern Baja Friday afternoon and then northern Mexico/far southern 
New Mexico Friday night and Saturday morning, ejecting out ahead of 
the main trough. Decent moisture contained with this low as PWs 
approach or slightly exceed .75 inches. Expect some showers to 
develop west of the RG Valley Friday afternoon and spread eastward 
Friday night with the help of the surface cold front. Good cold air 
aloft (500mb temps cooling about 5 deg) will aid in supplying modest 
amounts of CAPE and slightly negative LIs. So can't rule out an 
isolated thunderstorm with these showers. Low over Texas Panhandle 
by Saturday afternoon should end most showers, but the main trough 
from the Pac NW low quickly moves across the CWA Saturday night and 
Sunday. Thus, the mountains could see a few more showers lingering 
into Sunday morning. Snow levels over the mountains Saturday around 
9500 ft and falling to around 8500 ft overnight into Sunday morning. 
A couple inches of snow is possible at these elevations. Some breezy 
afternoon winds also possible Friday.

Monday through Wednesday...shortwave ridge transits across the area 
Monday behind the exiting trough. Next Pacific trough comes through 
Tuesday night and Wednesday. Main energy from this trough remains 
across Colorado and northern New Mexico with surface front through 
the area by Tuesday night. Chance of showers at this time limited to 
the mountains with breezy winds Tuesday night and Wednesday. 
Temperatures remain below normal for this period.

&&

.AVIATION...
(06Z TAFS) Issued at 934 PM MST Tue Nov 10 2026

VFR conditions through the period with SKC-SCT250. Winds variable 
AOB 7 knots becoming mainly northeast 7-10 knots Wednesday 
afternoon. Note: models show some low clouds/fog forming southern 
Luna, southern Dona Ana, and El Paso counties late tonight-hence 
there is a non-zero chance that KELP/KLRU could see some overnight
fog, but confidence still too low to include in TAFs.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1049 AM MST Tue Nov 10 2026

RH falls to the 20-25% range in portions of the Gila NF both this 
afternoon and again on Wednesday, but 20-ft. winds generally less 
than 8mph and very low ERC percentiles preclude wildfire spread 
risk. Generally poor ventilation rates today and Veterans' Day 
improve on Thursday, especially in the Gila. Vent rates trend up 
more broadly, to Fair to Good, for Friday to Sunday as rain chances 
return. A dusting of snow could occur on the highest peaks (above 10 
kft.).
